title: How to enlarge cursor in Zoom on Mac: simple steps for better visibility
metaTitle: How to Enlarge Cursor in Zoom on Mac: Simple Steps
description: Learn how to enlarge your cursor in Zoom on Mac by adjusting your system-wide accessibility settings to improve visibility during your video meetings.
intro: To enlarge your cursor in Zoom on a Mac, you must adjust your system-wide accessibility settings rather than looking within the Zoom application itself. Because Zoom inherits your macOS pointer configuration, changing your system settings will immediately increase the size of your cursor across all applications, including your Zoom meetings.
tldr: Open System Settings on your Mac.
Navigate to Accessibility and then Display.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preferred level.
Enable Shake mouse pointer to locate for easier tracking.

stats.label: Hybrid meeting participants reporting difficulty seeing content

blocks.text: Why adjust your cursor size for Zoom

Video meetings often require you to follow a presenter's screen or navigate complex interfaces in real time. If your cursor is small, it can easily get lost against busy backgrounds or high-resolution slides. This is especially true if you are sharing your own screen or teaching a class where others need to follow your actions.

Research into video conferencing shows that visual fatigue is a significant issue for frequent users. By making your cursor larger, you reduce the strain on your eyes. You also make it easier for your audience to track where you are pointing. This simple change is a foundational step in making your digital workspace more comfortable.
How to enlarge your cursor in macOS

Since Zoom does not have a dedicated setting for cursor size, you will use the macOS System Settings. This change applies globally, so your cursor will be larger in every app you use, not just Zoom. Follow these steps to make the change.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Click on the Accessibility tab in the left sidebar.
Click on Display to open your visual settings.
Find the Pointer section near the bottom of the window.
Drag the Pointer size slider to the right to enlarge your cursor.

blocks.text: You will notice the change instantly. You do not need to restart Zoom for this to take effect. If you find the cursor is still hard to see, you can adjust the slider further until it feels right for your screen resolution.

Sometimes, even a larger cursor can disappear during a fast-paced meeting. macOS includes a feature called Shake to Locate. When you enable this, you can quickly wiggle your mouse or trackpad back and forth. The cursor will temporarily grow much larger, making it impossible to miss.

items: Go back to System Settings > Accessibility > Display.
Locate the Shake mouse pointer to locate toggle.
Ensure the switch is turned on.

blocks.text: This feature is perfect for when you are presenting and need to draw attention to a specific button or menu item on your screen. It is a subtle but effective way to improve your presentation style without needing complex tools.

Beyond the cursor, there are other ways to make your Zoom experience more accessible. If you find it difficult to read text, you might consider using the built-in Zoom screen magnifier. This is different from the Zoom application and is also found in your Accessibility settings.

To enable screen magnification, go to System Settings > Accessibility > Zoom. You can set it to use a scroll gesture with a modifier key. For example, holding the Control key while scrolling with your trackpad will magnify the area under your cursor. This is a powerful tool for showing small details during a screen share.

Users often look inside the Zoom settings menu for cursor options. Because Zoom relies on the operating system for input rendering, you will not find these controls in the app. If you change your cursor size and do not see the change, try closing and reopening your meeting. In rare cases, the system needs a moment to propagate the change to active windows.

Another common issue is confusing the Mac's system-level accessibility zoom with the Zoom video app. If you search for Zoom in your system settings, you will see both the video app and the accessibility features. Always look for the Accessibility category when you want to change how your screen behaves.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor size only for Zoom?
faq.answer: No, macOS controls the cursor size system-wide. Any change you make will affect the cursor in all applications, including Zoom.

faq.question: Will a larger cursor affect my screen sharing?
faq.answer: Yes, your audience will see the larger cursor. This is often helpful for presentations, as it makes it easier for viewers to follow your movements.

faq.question: Where is the cursor setting in macOS?
faq.answer: It is located in System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Pointer.

task: Enlarge your mouse cursor using system-wide accessibility settings on macOS.
appliesTo: macOS Sonoma, Sequoia, and later versions.
requirements: A Mac running a modern version of macOS.

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen and select System Settings.

steps.name: Access Accessibility
steps.text: Click the Accessibility tab located in the left-hand sidebar.

steps.name: Open Display Settings
steps.text: Click the Display option to view your visual accessibility settings.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer Size
steps.text: Locate the Pointer section and move the slider to the right to increase the cursor size.

troubleshooting.fix: Ensure you have clicked out of the slider and wait a moment for the system to apply the change.
Ensure you are in the Display section of the Accessibility menu in System Settings.
